body:
다음 글의 분위기로 가장 적절한 것은?

A freezing wind sweeps through the dark streets. Pearl Kendrick and Grace Eldering walk from one house to another, carrying lamps and collecting samples from children with pertussis. Inside the homes, the children cough without pause and fight for every breath.
solution: 매서운 바람, 어두운 거리, 심한 기침과 호흡 곤란이 나타난다. 따라서 글의 분위기는 밝거나 평화롭기보다 암울하고 고통스럽다.

body:
다음 글에 드러난 전반적인 분위기로 가장 적절한 것은?

The laboratory work is over, but Kendrick and Eldering do not rest. In the fading light, they head toward the homes of seriously ill children. The weak light of their lamps and the sound of uncontrolled coughing fill the evening.
solution: 연구를 마친 뒤에도 두 사람이 중병에 걸린 아이들을 찾아가고, 희미한 불빛과 거친 기침 소리가 제시된다. 이러한 표현들은 진지하고 침울한 분위기를 형성한다.

body:
다음 글의 분위기로 가장 적절한 것은?

Beyond the laboratory lies a society damaged by the Great Depression. Banks have failed, industries have collapsed, and many parents have no work. As their sick children struggle to breathe, the parents tell Kendrick and Eldering their painful stories.
solution: 경제적 붕괴와 실업뿐 아니라 아이들의 위태로운 상태와 부모들의 고통까지 묘사된다. 따라서 절망적이고 슬픈 분위기가 가장 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 분위기로 가장 적절한 것은?

Night settles over the world outside the laboratory. Although the day's official duties have ended, Kendrick and Eldering begin another demanding task. They move through the cold darkness to reach children whose violent coughing leaves them hardly able to breathe.
solution: 밤과 추위 속에서 두 사람이 호흡 곤란을 겪는 아이들을 찾아가는 상황에는 긴박함이 있다. 동시에 병세가 매우 심각하므로 엄숙하고 무거운 분위기도 드러난다.

body:
다음 글의 분위기로 가장 적절한 것은?

A lamp throws only a weak circle of light as the two researchers enter yet another home. An unemployed parent speaks of hardship while a child nearby is seized by repeated coughing. No one in the room can be certain that the child will survive.
solution: 희미한 불빛, 실직한 부모의 고난, 아이의 생존이 불확실한 상황이 결합되어 있다. 이는 암담하면서도 불안한 분위기를 만든다.

body:
다음 글에서 지배적인 분위기로 가장 적절한 것은?

Kendrick and Eldering continue their visits even after darkness covers the streets. Their steady work might suggest hope, yet the scenes before them are harsh: ruined livelihoods, frightened parents, and children weakened by endless coughing. The small lamps reveal suffering far greater than their light can soften.
solution: 두 연구자의 꾸준한 행동에서 희망을 일부 느낄 수 있지만, 지문은 주로 생계의 붕괴와 부모의 두려움, 아이들의 고통을 강조한다. 따라서 지배적인 분위기는 암울하다는 판단이 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 분위기에 대한 설명으로 가장 적절한 것은?

The cold wind and deepening darkness surround the researchers as they leave the laboratory. In each home, they carefully gather samples while listening to parents who have lost their jobs. Their disciplined movements contrast sharply with the helpless gasps of the sick children.
choices: It is peaceful because the researchers work carefully.
It is amusing because the two women repeatedly visit homes.
It is celebratory because scientific work is being performed.
It is tense and solemn despite the researchers' controlled behavior.
It is dreamy because darkness hides the suffering around them.
solution: 연구자들의 행동은 침착하고 체계적이지만, 주변에는 실업과 아이들의 호흡 곤란이 존재한다. 침착한 행동만 보고 평화로운 분위기로 판단하면 안 되며, 전체적으로는 긴장되고 엄숙하다.

body:
다음 글의 분위기 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?

At first, the end of the workday seems to promise a pause. Soon, however, Kendrick and Eldering step into the bitter wind and begin visiting families affected by pertussis. As they hear the parents' accounts and watch the children struggle for air, any sense of relief disappears.
choices: from expectation of rest to grave distress
from intense fear to complete amusement
from public celebration to private peace
from deep sorrow to romantic excitement
from scientific curiosity to cheerful pride
solution: 처음에는 일과가 끝나 휴식이 예상되는 듯하다. 그러나 두 사람이 아픈 아이들과 절망한 부모들을 마주하면서 분위기가 무겁고 고통스럽게 바뀐다.

body:
다음 글의 지배적인 분위기를 나타내는 영어 형용사 두 개를 본문에 근거하여 쓰시오. (두 단어는 and로 연결할 것.)

Outside, failed banks and collapsed industry have left families without security. Inside their homes, parents speak in strained voices while their children cough until breathing itself becomes a struggle. Kendrick and Eldering work under dim lamplight, surrounded by suffering they cannot immediately end.
solution: 경제적 붕괴와 불안정한 가정 형편은 bleak한 분위기를 조성한다. 또한 아이들의 심한 기침과 즉시 끝낼 수 없는 고통은 distressing한 분위기를 강화한다.

body:
다음 글의 분위기를 가장 잘 나타내는 영어 형용사 두 개를 쓰시오. 첫 번째 단어는 상황의 시간적 압박을, 두 번째 단어는 사건의 무거움을 나타내야 한다. (두 단어는 and로 연결할 것.)

There is no time for a quiet evening. The researchers must reach the homes while the infected children remain in danger, collect what they need, and face one severe coughing attack after another. Each desperate breath makes the importance of their task impossible to ignore.
solution: 위험에 처한 아이들을 서둘러 찾아가야 하므로 시간적 압박을 나타내는 urgent가 적절하다. 심각한 병세와 절박한 호흡은 사건의 무거움을 나타내는 grave와 연결된다.

body:
다음 글의 분위기 변화를 ‘처음의 예상’과 ‘이후의 지배적 분위기’가 드러나도록 영어로 쓰시오. (from A to B의 형식으로 쓸 것.)

The close of the laboratory day briefly suggests that the two women may stop working. Instead, they enter the freezing darkness and encounter unemployed parents, uncontrolled coughing, and children barely holding on to life. The expected comfort of evening gives way completely.
solution: 일과 종료는 처음에 휴식을 기대하게 하므로 restful로 표현할 수 있다. 이후에는 실업한 부모와 생명이 위태로운 아이들이 부각되므로 지배적인 분위기는 somber로 바뀐다.

body:
다음 글에 드러난 Picasso의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?

At Arias’s barbershop, Picasso was often served before the other customers. He did not like making them wait. When Arias suggested cutting his hair at Picasso’s home instead, Picasso gladly agreed.
solution: Picasso는 다른 손님들을 기다리게 하는 상황을 불편하게 여겼다. Arias가 집에서 이발해 주겠다고 제안하자 기쁘게 받아들였으므로 ‘uncomfortable → pleased’가 적절하다.

body:
다음 글에 나타난 Picasso의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?

Picasso noticed that customers at the barbershop had to wait whenever they allowed him to go first. This troubled him. Later, Arias visited Picasso’s house, and the two men spent more time together as close friends.
solution: 처음에 Picasso는 자신 때문에 다른 손님들이 기다리는 것을 난처하게 생각했다. 이후 Arias와 집에서 편안하게 어울리는 친구가 되었으므로 ‘embarrassed → comfortable’가 알맞다.

body:
다음 글에 드러난 Picasso의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?

Picasso felt bad about receiving special treatment in Arias’s shop. Arias understood him and offered another way to provide his services. Picasso welcomed the idea, and their relationship eventually developed into a warm friendship.
solution: 특별 대우로 다른 사람들이 기다리는 상황에서 Picasso는 마음이 불편했다. Arias의 배려를 기쁘게 받아들이고 우정까지 깊어졌으므로 ‘uneasy → delighted’가 정답이다.

body:
다음 글의 흐름을 고려할 때, Picasso의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?

Whenever Picasso entered the barbershop, people gave up their turns for him. Instead of enjoying the privilege, he became conscious of the inconvenience caused to them. Arias recognized this and began visiting Picasso’s house. As time passed, Picasso openly welcomed Arias and enjoyed talking with him for hours.
solution: Picasso는 다른 손님들에게 불편을 주는 것 같아 미안하고 부담스러워했다. 이후 Arias와 가까운 친구가 되어 오랜 시간 편안하게 대화했으므로 ‘guilty → at ease’가 적절하다.

body:
다음 글에 나타난 Picasso의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?

Being placed ahead of everyone else at the shop was a burden to Picasso. Arias then offered to come to his home, and Picasso accepted without hesitation. Their meetings were no longer limited to haircuts; Picasso came to regard Arias’s visits as a welcome reminder of Spain.
solution: Picasso는 이발소에서 우선 대접받는 것을 부담스럽게 느꼈다. 나중에는 Arias가 자신의 집에 오면 고향 스페인에 돌아온 듯한 위안을 느꼈으므로 ‘burdened → comforted’가 정답이다.

body:
다음 글의 Picasso에 관한 내용으로 보아 그의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?

Picasso could not relax when his presence delayed the other customers. After Arias found a considerate solution, the two exchanged more than services and artworks: they shared meals, visits, and long conversations. Picasso was happy to have Arias around him.
solution: 처음의 Picasso는 다른 손님들을 지연시키는 상황 때문에 마음이 편하지 않았다. 이후 Arias와 식사와 대화를 함께하는 가까운 사이가 되었으므로 심경은 ‘troubled → affectionate’로 변했다고 볼 수 있다.

body:
다음 글에 드러난 Picasso의 심경 변화를 가장 적절하게 나타낸 것은?

The customers’ kindness at the shop had an unintended effect on Picasso: their willingness to put him first made him aware that they were losing time because of him. Arias removed this concern by visiting Picasso’s home. In the course of their growing friendship, Picasso told Arias that his presence made Spain feel close again.
choices: He felt honored by the customers and then became tired of Arias.
He felt responsible for others’ inconvenience and then emotionally reassured.
He felt suspicious of Arias and then became dependent on his services.
He felt ignored in the shop and then became proud of his fame.
He felt disappointed by the customers and then regretted leaving Spain.
solution: 손님들의 양보는 호의였지만 Picasso에게는 그들을 기다리게 한다는 부담을 주었다. 이후 Arias와의 우정은 Picasso가 스페인을 가까이 느끼게 하는 정서적 위안이 되었다. 따라서 책임감에서 비롯된 불편함이 안정감으로 바뀌었다는 ②가 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 사건 전개에 따른 Picasso의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?

Picasso was uneasy about the price others paid for his special treatment at the barbershop—their time. Arias’s proposal allowed him to receive the same services without delaying anyone. Later, Arias visited even when no haircut was needed, and Picasso welcomed these occasions because Arias brought him a sense of his homeland.
solution: Picasso는 특별 대우로 다른 사람의 시간을 빼앗는다는 점을 의식해 불편해했다. 집에서 서비스를 받게 되면서 그 부담이 해소되었고, 이후 Arias에게 고향의 정서를 느끼며 애착을 갖게 되었다. 따라서 ‘self-conscious → relieved → attached’가 사건의 흐름과 일치한다.

body:
다음 글에 나타난 Picasso의 심경 변화를 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.

The other customers’ repeated willingness to let Picasso go first did not make him proud. Rather, he was disturbed by the delay imposed on them. Arias understood the problem and began providing his services at Picasso’s house. As their friendship deepened, Picasso associated Arias’s company with the warmth of Spain.

<조건>
- ‘불편한’과 ‘위안을 받은’의 의미를 나타내는 영어 단어를 차례로 쓸 것
- 각 단어는 본문에 사용되지 않은 한 단어일 것
- ‘단어 → 단어’의 형식으로 쓸 것
solution: 처음에는 다른 손님들이 지체되는 것 때문에 Picasso가 불편함을 느꼈다. 이후 Arias와의 우정에서 고향의 따뜻함을 느끼며 위안을 얻었다. 두 심경을 본문에 없는 단어로 나타내면 ‘uneasy → comforted’이다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 Picasso의 처음과 나중 심경을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.

What seemed to be a privilege at the shop was actually a source of concern for Picasso, since it lengthened everyone else’s wait. The concern disappeared when Arias offered to work at Picasso’s home. Eventually, the visits became friendly gatherings, and Arias’s presence gave Picasso the feeling of being connected to Spain again.

Picasso felt (A)________ about inconveniencing others but later felt emotionally (B)________ in Arias’s company.

<조건>
- (A), (B)에 각각 한 단어를 쓸 것
- (A)는 g로, (B)는 r로 시작할 것
- 문법적으로 felt 뒤에 올 수 있는 형용사를 쓸 것
solution: 다른 사람들을 기다리게 한다는 점에서 처음 심경은 ‘guilty’로 표현할 수 있다. Arias와 함께하며 고향과 연결된 듯한 정서적 안정을 얻었으므로 나중 심경은 ‘reassured’가 적절하다. 두 단어 모두 felt의 보어로 쓰이는 형용사이다.

body:
다음 글의 마지막 문장을 완성하도록 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.

At first, the customers’ kindness only heightened Picasso’s awareness that they had to wait longer for him. Arias solved the difficulty by changing where the service was provided. Their contact then grew into a friendship marked by exchanged works, shared meals, and lengthy conversations. Arias’s visits even revived in Picasso the familiar feeling of Spain.

Thus, Picasso’s feeling changed from social (A)________ to emotional (B)________.

<조건>
- (A), (B)에 각각 하나의 영어 명사를 쓸 것
- (A)는 d로, (B)는 c로 시작할 것
- 두 단어 모두 문맥상 Picasso의 심리 상태를 나타낼 것
solution: 처음 Picasso는 특별 대우로 다른 사람들을 기다리게 하는 사회적 상황에서 불편함을 느꼈다. 나중에는 Arias의 우정을 통해 스페인을 떠올리며 정서적 위안을 얻었다. 따라서 명사 형태인 ‘discomfort, comfort’가 두 빈칸에 알맞다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

A person who wants to exercise regularly may place workout clothes beside the bed before going to sleep. In the morning, the clothes act as a cue, and getting started requires less preparation. In this way, (A)the path to the desired behavior becomes shorter. When a habit is easy to begin, it is more likely to be repeated.
choices: 운동의 목표를 더 자주 변경하게 된다.
원하는 행동을 시작하는 데 필요한 수고가 줄어든다.
행동의 결과보다 준비 과정이 더 중요해진다.
운동을 해야 한다는 욕구가 완전히 사라진다.
새로운 습관을 일상적인 활동과 분리하게 된다.
solution: 운동복을 미리 준비하면 아침에 운동을 시작하기 위한 준비 과정이 줄어든다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분은 원하는 행동을 실행하는 데 필요한 수고가 감소한다는 뜻이다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

After completing a new habit, some people put a mark on a calendar. Each mark shows that they have followed their plan once more. Although the mark itself is simple, it gives them an immediate feeling of progress. Thus, (A)the record becomes a small reward rather than a mere piece of information.
choices: 기록은 장기 목표를 더 어렵게 만든다.
기록은 성취감을 주어 행동의 반복을 돕는다.
solution: 달력의 표시는 계획을 실천했다는 진전을 즉시 보여 준다. 이로부터 얻는 작은 성취감이 보상으로 작용하여 습관을 계속하게 한다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

A habit loop begins with a cue and continues through craving and response to reward. If these steps connect smoothly, a person does not have to make a completely new decision each time. With enough repetition, (A)the cue can set the rest of the process in motion.
choices: 신호가 뒤따르는 습관 과정을 자연스럽게 시작하게 할 수 있다.
신호가 행동의 보상을 불필요하게 만들 수 있다.
습관을 형성하려면 매번 새로운 결정을 내려야 한다.
solution: 습관 고리에서 신호는 욕구와 반응, 보상으로 이어지는 과정의 출발점이다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분은 신호가 이후 단계를 자연스럽게 작동시킨다는 의미이다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

Suppose a person plans to record a completed habit whenever it occurs. The record does more than preserve a memory of the behavior. It turns otherwise invisible improvement into something that can be seen immediately. As a result, (A)progress does not have to wait for the final goal to announce itself.
choices: 최종 목표는 습관 형성 과정에서 제외되어야 한다.
행동을 기록하면 최종 결과를 미리 정확히 예측할 수 있다.
작은 향상도 기록을 통해 즉시 확인될 수 있다.
진정한 성취는 모든 목표를 달성한 뒤에만 느낄 수 있다.
습관의 결과가 보이지 않을수록 행동을 유지하기 쉽다.
solution: 기록은 눈에 잘 보이지 않는 작은 향상을 즉시 확인하게 해 준다. 그러므로 최종 목표를 달성하기 전에도 자신의 진전을 인식할 수 있다는 의미이다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

People sometimes design a new habit that demands too many choices and too much preparation. Even if they strongly desire the result, the complicated response can interrupt the habit loop. A simpler response, however, allows the loop to run with less conscious control. In habit formation, therefore, (A)good intentions need a smooth road.
choices: 강한 의지만 있다면 행동의 복잡성은 문제가 되지 않는다.
좋은 의도는 실행하기 쉬운 행동 구조의 도움을 받아야 한다.
습관을 유지하려면 의식적인 판단의 횟수를 늘려야 한다.
행동이 어려울수록 결과에 대한 욕구가 강해진다.
습관의 성공 여부는 목표의 가치로만 결정된다.
solution: 좋은 의도나 강한 욕구만으로는 복잡한 행동을 꾸준히 반복하기 어렵다. ‘smooth road’는 준비와 선택이 적어 행동을 쉽게 실행할 수 있는 조건을 비유한다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

A person may connect a new habit to an action that already occurs every day. The familiar action then serves as a reliable cue for the new response. Because the person does not need to search for a separate time to begin, the new behavior can enter the daily routine more naturally. In this sense, (A)an old routine can carry a new habit.
choices: 기존 일과는 새로운 행동의 보상을 대신할 수 있다.
새 습관은 기존 일과가 사라진 뒤에 형성될 수 있다.
새로운 행동은 일상에서 분리할수록 더 쉽게 기억된다.
익숙한 일과를 신호로 삼으면 새 습관을 자연스럽게 실행할 수 있다.
기존 일과를 반복하면 새로운 목표를 세울 필요가 없어진다.
solution: 매일 하는 익숙한 행동은 새 습관을 시작하게 하는 안정적인 신호가 될 수 있다. 따라서 밑줄 친 표현은 기존 일과에 새 행동을 연결하면 그 실행이 쉬워진다는 뜻이다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

A person carefully tracks a new habit but chooses a response that requires considerable preparation each time. The record may provide satisfaction after the behavior, yet the person still frequently fails to begin it. This shows that a reward can strengthen a completed response but cannot make an unnecessarily difficult response easy. In other words, (A)the final link cannot repair every weakness earlier in the chain.
choices: 충분한 보상이 주어지면 복잡한 행동도 자동으로 시작된다.
행동의 결과를 기록하면 신호와 욕구는 더 이상 필요하지 않다.
보상은 습관 고리의 앞 단계에 있는 실행상의 어려움을 모두 해결할 수 없다.
습관 고리에서는 마지막 단계만 행동의 반복에 영향을 준다.
반응이 어려울수록 행동을 마친 뒤의 만족감도 반드시 커진다.
solution: ‘final link’는 습관 고리의 마지막 단계인 보상을 가리킨다. 보상은 완료된 행동의 반복을 돕지만, 그 이전 반응 단계가 지나치게 어렵다는 문제까지 없애지는 못한다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

Two people may perform the same new behavior, but only one connects it with a desired identity. For that person, each repetition is not merely the completion of a task; it is also evidence of the kind of person the individual hopes to become. The behavior and the identity then support each other. Thus, (A)repetition can serve as a vote for the self one is building.
choices: 행동의 반복은 자신이 지향하는 정체성을 뒷받침하는 증거가 될 수 있다.
바람직한 정체성은 행동을 반복하지 않아도 즉시 완성될 수 있다.
같은 행동을 하는 사람들은 반드시 동일한 정체성을 갖게 된다.
새 습관의 가치는 다른 사람의 평가를 받을 때 결정된다.
정체성을 먼저 확정하면 습관 고리의 보상은 필요하지 않다.
solution: 여기서 ‘vote’는 실제 투표가 아니라 반복되는 행동이 원하는 정체성을 지지하는 증거가 된다는 비유이다. 행동을 거듭할수록 자신이 되고자 하는 사람의 모습이 강화된다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

An immediate reward is useful because it links satisfaction closely to a completed response. Yet the reward should support, not replace, the behavior that the person wants to maintain. If attention shifts entirely to collecting marks in a tracker, the record may continue even when the intended response is performed carelessly. Therefore, (A)the sign of progress must not become a substitute for progress itself.
choices: 습관을 기록하려면 행동의 질보다 표시의 수를 우선해야 한다.
즉각적인 만족을 주는 기록은 장기적인 습관과 양립할 수 없다.
기록이 계속된다면 실제 행동을 수행했는지는 중요하지 않다.
진전의 표시는 원하는 행동을 성실히 수행한 경우에만 보상으로 기능해야 한다.
습관 추적은 행동의 실제 향상보다 기록 자체를 목표로 삼아야 한다.
solution: ‘sign of progress’는 습관 추적기에 남긴 표시이고, ‘progress itself’는 실제로 원하는 행동을 수행하고 향상하는 것이다. 기록만 늘리는 것이 실제 실천을 대신해서는 안 된다는 의미이므로 ④가 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 (A)가 의미하는 바를 우리말로 쓰시오.

A person wants a new behavior to become automatic and therefore makes the response extremely easy. This helps the behavior begin, but the person gives no attention to what happens afterward. There is neither a visible record of progress nor a satisfying result connected to completion. The behavior soon loses its attraction. This case suggests that (A)removing the hill does not by itself give the traveler a reason to return.
answer: 행동을 쉽게 만드는 것만으로는 습관의 반복이 보장되지 않으며, 반복을 위해서는 만족스러운 보상도 필요하다는 뜻
solution: ‘removing the hill’은 반응에 필요한 노력을 줄여 행동을 쉽게 만드는 것을 뜻한다. ‘a reason to return’은 행동을 다시 하게 하는 보상을 의미하므로, 쉬운 실행과 만족스러운 보상이 함께 필요하다는 내용이다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 (A)가 의미하는 바를 우리말로 쓰시오.

A habit tracker can offer immediate satisfaction, but its deeper value lies in what the repeated marks reveal. A single mark says only that the behavior occurred once. As the marks accumulate, however, they show that the person is repeatedly acting in accordance with a chosen identity. The tracker then connects present action, visible progress, and identity. In this way, (A)the marks are both footprints and a mirror.
answer: 기록은 행동이 이어져 온 과정을 보여 주는 동시에 반복을 통해 형성되는 자신의 정체성을 확인하게 한다는 뜻
solution: ‘footprints’는 지금까지 행동을 반복해 온 과정과 진전의 흔적을 의미한다. ‘mirror’는 그 반복이 드러내는 현재의 정체성을 비유하므로, 기록이 진행 과정과 정체성을 함께 보여 준다는 뜻이다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 나머지 넷과 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은?

Citizen scientists are ordinary people who want to help science. <u>ⓐThey</u> take an interest in scientific research without necessarily having science degrees. Their curiosity encourages <u>ⓑthem</u> to participate. The discovery of STEVE shows that <u>ⓒthey</u> can make valuable contributions. Several theories about STEVE exist, but none of <u>ⓓthem</u> have been proved certain. There is still much to learn, and citizen scientists can help. A white lab coat is not necessary for <u>ⓔthem</u> to contribute.
solution: ⓓthem은 바로 앞의 several theories about STEVE를 가리킨다. 나머지 네 표현은 모두 과학 연구에 참여하는 일반인인 citizen scientists를 가리킨다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 나머지 넷과 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은?

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 나머지 넷과 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은?

Citizen scientists need not be professional scientists. <u>ⓐThey</u> may have no science degrees, but <u>ⓑthey</u> can still contribute to research. There are many theories about STEVE, and scientists have not proved any of <u>ⓒthem</u> certain. This leaves an interesting mystery for further research. Citizen scientists can take part because curiosity gives <u>ⓓthem</u> a reason to learn. A desire to understand the world can lead <u>ⓔthem</u> into science.
solution: ⓒthem은 STEVE에 관한 many theories를 가리킨다. 나머지 표현들은 과학 학위가 없어도 연구에 기여할 수 있는 citizen scientists를 가리킨다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 나머지 넷과 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은?

The aurora chasers who discovered STEVE were dedicated observers. Experts recognize that the discovery belongs to <u>ⓐthem</u>. These experts have acknowledged the importance of the discovery, and <u>ⓑthey</u> give credit to its original discoverers. Without the aurora chasers, the phenomenon might have gone unnoticed. The decision to keep the name Steve honors <u>ⓒthem</u>. Although the name is now written in capital letters, its continued use recognizes what <u>ⓓthey</u> achieved. In this way, <u>ⓔthey</u> remain connected with the name of the phenomenon.
solution: ⓑthey의 선행사는 바로 앞 문장의 주어인 These experts이다. ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 STEVE를 발견한 aurora chasers를 가리킨다. 전문가와 최초 발견자의 역할을 구분해야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 나머지 넷과 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은?

Citizen scientists enter research because of their interest in the world. Science degrees are not necessary for <u>ⓐthem</u> to make useful contributions. The aurora chasers' discovery of STEVE illustrates the value of participation by ordinary people. Many theories now concern this phenomenon, but none of <u>ⓑthem</u> have been established as certain. By volunteering their time, <u>ⓔthey</u> may contribute to a future scientific achievement.
solution: ⓑthem은 앞 문장의 Many theories를 가리킨다. 나머지 네 표현은 모두 citizen scientists를 가리키며, 중간에 STEVE와 그에 관한 이론이 언급되어도 뒤에서 시민 과학자로 화제가 돌아온다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 나머지 넷과 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은?

There are many theories about STEVE. None of <u>ⓐthem</u> have been proved certain. Scientists and citizens continue to work together, but the existence of these theories does not mean that <u>ⓑthey</u> are established explanations. To call <u>ⓒthem</u> interesting is therefore different from calling them certain. The people studying STEVE are learning more about the phenomenon as <u>ⓓthey</u> continue their collaboration. Yet the theories remain theories: interest in <u>ⓔthem</u> should not be confused with proof.
solution: ⓓthey는 해당 문장의 주어인 The people studying STEVE를 가리킨다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ는 모두 STEVE에 관한 이론들을 가리킨다. ⓑ는 가까운 위치의 scientists and citizens가 아니라 these theories를 받는다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 나머지 넷과 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은?

The people who first discovered STEVE were the dedicated members of an aurora chasers group. It is <u>ⓐthey</u>, experts acknowledge, who deserve credit for the discovery. That acknowledgment comes from experts, but it concerns the achievement of the original discoverers. Had it not been for <u>ⓑthem</u>, STEVE might have remained unnoticed. Keeping the name Steve honors <u>ⓒthem</u>, even though the name now appears in capital letters. The experts who recognize this contribution deserve a clear distinction from its makers: <u>ⓓthey</u> acknowledge the discovery, whereas the aurora chasers made it. The credit given to the aurora chasers therefore reflects what <u>ⓔthey</u> actually achieved.
solution: ⓓthey는 콜론 앞 문장의 주어인 The experts who recognize this contribution을 가리킨다. 나머지 네 표현은 모두 최초 발견자인 오로라 추적자 모임의 헌신적인 구성원들을 가리킨다. 전문가들은 발견의 공로를 인정하는 주체이고, 오로라 추적자들은 실제 발견의 주체이다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 나머지 넷과 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은?

The theories about STEVE are interesting, but calling <u>ⓐthem</u> interesting does not establish their certainty. Scientists and citizens who continue to study the phenomenon are learning more about it; nevertheless, none of these theories have been proved certain. Whatever the interest <u>ⓑthey</u> attract, the theories must still be distinguished from established knowledge. Those involved in the research continue to collaborate, and <u>ⓒthey</u> are learning more about STEVE every day. This continuing work does not alter the present status of the theories: none of <u>ⓓthem</u> can yet be described as certainly proved. Referring to <u>ⓔthem</u> as theories preserves that distinction.
solution: ⓒthey는 연구에 참여하는 사람들을 뜻하는 Those involved in the research를 가리킨다. 나머지 네 표현은 모두 STEVE에 관한 이론들을 가리킨다. ⓑthey는 삽입된 절 안에서 the theories를 받으므로 연구자들을 가리키지 않는다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 나머지 넷과 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은?

Professional scientists are not the only people who can contribute to science. Although <u>ⓐthey</u> are professionals, scientific participation is also open to ordinary people. Such ordinary participants are called citizen scientists. What makes <u>ⓑthem</u> citizen scientists is their desire to help advance science in areas that interest them. Science degrees are not a requirement for <u>ⓒthem</u> to make valuable contributions. Nor does the absence of a long, white lab coat mean that <u>ⓓthey</u> have nothing to offer. The discovery of STEVE illustrates why the contribution of ordinary participants deserves recognition. Curiosity and a willingness to volunteer time can give <u>ⓔthem</u> a place in scientific research.
solution: ⓐthey는 첫 문장의 Professional scientists를 가리킨다. ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 시민 과학자인 일반인 참여자들을 가리킨다. 첫 문장의 not the only는 전문 과학자 외에도 기여할 사람이 있다는 뜻이며, ⓐ의 지칭 대상을 바꾸지는 않는다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 나머지 넷과 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은?

The name Steve was kept to honor the aurora chasers responsible for the discovery. The experts who have acknowledged the discoverers' contribution make a claim about credit: it is the dedicated members of the aurora chasers group, rather than the experts themselves, who deserve it. To say that the phenomenon might have remained unnoticed without <u>ⓐthem</u> is to recognize the importance of those members. Interesting theories about STEVE also exist, but none of <u>ⓑthem</u>, however interesting, have been proved certain. Uncertainty about these theories does not change who first noticed the phenomenon. The discoverers retain that credit because <u>ⓒthey</u> made the discovery, regardless of how much remains unexplained. The continued use of the name honors <u>ⓓthem</u>; writing it in capitals does not remove its connection with the people whose contribution it recognizes. It is therefore the original aurora chasers whose achievement is acknowledged when <u>ⓔthey</u> are credited with discovering STEVE.
solution: ⓑthem은 STEVE에 관한 interesting theories를 가리킨다. 나머지는 모두 STEVE를 처음 발견한 오로라 추적자 모임의 구성원들을 가리킨다. ⓐ는 가까이에 언급된 experts가 아니라 발견에 공로가 있는 those members를 받으며, 발견의 공로와 이론의 확실성은 구분해야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 나머지 넷과 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은?

What the scientists and citizens studying STEVE have not yet established is the certainty of any of the theories about it. Interesting though <u>ⓐthey</u> may be, these theories remain unproved. The people engaged in the continuing research are learning more about the phenomenon, but describing the theories as interesting does not make <u>ⓑthem</u> certain. This is a distinction between the status of explanations and the activity of the people considering them. Those working together to solve the mystery continue their collaboration, and the more <u>ⓒthey</u> learn about STEVE, the more knowledge of the phenomenon they gain. As for the theories, however, none of <u>ⓓthem</u> have been proved certain. Their interest and their certainty are separate matters: however much the former invites further study, it cannot by itself establish the latter. Thus, when the theories are mentioned, <u>ⓔthey</u> should still be understood as explanations whose certainty has not been established.
solution: ⓒthey는 Those working together to solve the mystery, 즉 함께 연구하는 과학자와 시민들을 가리킨다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 STEVE에 관한 이론들을 가리킨다. ⓐ는 양보절 도치 구문에 쓰였으며, 뒤의 these theories가 지칭 대상을 분명하게 해 준다.

I am writing to apply for the weekend volunteer position at the city aquarium. At school, I participated in a project examining how water temperature affects algae growth. Through this project, I learned to record observations carefully and explain scientific results clearly. I have also attached my résumé and a recommendation from my science teacher. I would be grateful for an opportunity to contribute to the aquarium while learning more about animal care.

body:
다음 글이 실리기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

Pollination

Pollination is the movement of pollen from one part of a flower to another, allowing many plants to produce seeds. The pollen may be carried by wind, water, or animals. Bees are particularly important pollinators because pollen often sticks to their bodies while they collect food from flowers. When they visit another flower, some of that pollen may be transferred. Many wild plants and crops depend on this process. Pollination is different from the later process in which the male and female cells of a plant join.

Related topics: Honeybees · Flowers · Plant reproduction

This study investigated whether the timing of a short outdoor break influences students’ concentration. Three hundred students from five high schools participated for twelve weeks. One group walked outdoors for ten minutes before its first afternoon class, while another group took the same walk after classes had ended. A third group followed its ordinary schedule. The participants completed computer-based attention tasks at the beginning and end of the study. Their sleeping hours and physical activity outside school were also recorded. The group that walked before afternoon class showed greater improvement in attention scores than either of the other groups, but no meaningful difference was found in semester grades. The results suggest that the timing of a brief outdoor break may affect immediate concentration. Further studies are required to determine whether the effect continues over a longer period.

Students often asked me how scientists can learn about stars that no human being can visit. Their questions persuaded me that an introduction to astronomy should begin not with a list of facts but with the process of finding answers. For that reason, every chapter in this volume opens with a question raised in one of my classes. The first few chapters can be read without previous scientific training; later chapters build on the ideas introduced earlier. This is neither an encyclopedia of the universe nor a guide to observing every object in the night sky. My hope is simply that readers will understand how evidence can lead us from a familiar question to an unexpected conclusion. I owe particular thanks to the students who allowed their questions to guide the shape of this work and to the editor whose careful suggestions improved every chapter.

The city council is right to examine public spending carefully, especially when several essential services require additional support. Its proposal to reduce library funding, however, mistakes a decline in printed-book loans for a decline in the value of libraries themselves. The council’s report also shows that visits to local libraries have risen and that their computers and study areas are used more frequently than before. These services matter most to residents who cannot easily obtain Internet access or quiet working space elsewhere. A responsible budget should reflect how an institution is actually used, not merely how many books leave its shelves. Before approving the reduction, council members should consider less harmful savings and listen to residents at the upcoming public hearing. We therefore call on the council to revise its proposal.

(A)
A recent column argues that schools should replace most homework with optional activities because compulsory assignments create unnecessary pressure. The column is right that lengthy and repetitive tasks can harm students’ health. Yet it treats all homework as if it were equally ineffective. A short assignment closely connected to a lesson can reveal what students have not understood and give them a chance to practise independently. Schools should improve the quality of homework and limit its amount, not make it optional in nearly every case.

(B)
Our newspaper has repeatedly called for schools to reduce assignments that merely keep students busy. Nevertheless, eliminating required homework would deprive teachers of a useful educational tool. School leaders should establish limits on time and require teachers to explain the purpose of major assignments. Such a policy would protect students from excessive workloads while preserving carefully designed practice. We urge the district to adopt these standards before the next academic year.

Arguments about outdoor breaks at school often focus on whether such breaks improve academic grades. The investigation reported here began with a narrower question: can a brief walk help students concentrate during the class that immediately follows it? Students at four high schools completed the same attention task before and after a semester-long program. Their sleep and exercise outside school were recorded so that these factors could be considered. Those who took a short walk before afternoon lessons improved more on the attention task than those who followed their ordinary schedule, although the two groups did not differ significantly in overall grades. Because the participants were all high school students and the program lasted only one semester, the results should not be applied automatically to younger students or to long-term academic achievement.

Tardigrades can be found in a wide range of environments, but they are commonly discovered in the moisture surrounding moss and lichen. When this moisture disappears, they lose most of the water in their bodies and enter an inactive state in which their metabolism becomes extremely slow. This change enables them to survive severe cold and powerful radiation. Once water becomes available again, they absorb it and resume activity. Researchers are examining this survival mechanism because it may provide ideas for storing medicines in places where refrigeration is unavailable.

The mountain surrounding the facility remains naturally cold because of permafrost, and the entrance is located well above sea level. The seeds are kept at a very low temperature so that many of them can survive for long periods. Studies comparing members of the same bird species have shown that city birds often use higher notes than birds living in quiet forests. Certain species respond in other ways, such as increasing their volume or singing when the surroundings are less noisy. Such changes improve the chance that a signal will be heard. They do not, however, guarantee reproductive success, since females of some species seem more attracted to lower notes.

A decision can be costly even when no payment is required. Suppose a free lecture and a paid work shift take place at the same time. For a person who chooses the lecture, the relevant sacrifice may include the wages that the shift would have provided. Another person who had no work scheduled might give up only an evening of rest. Economists describe the value of the most valuable rejected option as the opportunity cost. Thus, two people may select the same activity but bear different opportunity costs. The concept identifies what is sacrificed; it does not, by itself, declare that either person's decision is mistaken.

After investing considerable time in an unsatisfying course, a student may feel compelled to continue simply because leaving would make the past effort seem wasted. A company may react similarly when it keeps supporting a failing project on the grounds that a great deal of money has already been spent. In both cases, the previous investment is unrecoverable regardless of the next decision. Treating that investment as a reason to continue is an example of the sunk cost fallacy. Avoiding the fallacy does not require abandoning every difficult undertaking. It requires comparing the future advantages and disadvantages of continuing with those of stopping.

In an experiment on chess memory, skilled players and beginners briefly viewed positions taken from actual matches. The skilled players reconstructed far more of the board correctly. The result changed when the pieces were placed in combinations that violated the familiar structure of real play: the difference between the two groups became much smaller. This suggests that the experts were not merely relying on an unusually powerful memory that worked equally well with all kinds of material. Long experience had allowed them to store recurring arrangements and recognize several related pieces as one organized pattern. What looked like superior memory was therefore closely tied to knowledge of the game.

Good decisions require attention to both what is given up and what can still be changed. Choosing a free event may involve sacrificing the most valuable alternative available at that time, such as paid work or needed rest. That sacrifice is the decision's opportunity cost, and it varies with the alternatives open to the person making the choice. By contrast, money or time already spent and impossible to recover is a sunk cost. A person who continues an unpleasant activity solely to justify such a past investment is allowing an irrelevant cost to control the decision. This does not mean that continuing is always irrational: it may be reasonable when the expected future benefits exceed the future costs. Nor do these concepts automatically select the best option, since people may value the available alternatives differently.

<보기>
ㄱ. 비용을 받지 않는 행사에는 어떤 형태의 비용도 존재하지 않는다.
ㄴ. 같은 행사에 참여해도 각자가 포기한 최선의 대안은 다를 수 있다.
ㄷ. 되돌려 받을 수 없는 과거의 지출은 현재 선택의 결정적 기준이 되어야 한다.
ㄹ. 매몰 비용의 오류를 피하려면 불쾌하거나 어려운 활동을 즉시 중단해야 한다.
ㅁ. 활동을 계속할지는 그 활동이 앞으로 가져올 비용과 이익을 고려하여 판단할 수 있다.
solution: ㄴ은 개인마다 이용 가능한 대안이 다를 수 있다는 점에서, ㅁ은 미래의 비용과 이익을 비교해야 한다는 점에서 추론 가능하다. ㄱ은 무료 활동에도 기회비용이 있다는 설명과 어긋나며, ㄷ은 회수 불가능한 비용을 판단 기준에서 배제해야 한다는 취지에 반한다. 계속하는 선택도 미래 이익이 크다면 합리적일 수 있으므로 ㄹ 역시 추론할 수 없어 정답은 ⑤이다.

body:
다음 글의 표시된 다섯 문장 중 글 전체의 주제문으로 가장 알맞은 것은?

ⓐ A reader searching for a particular word may move through a page quite quickly. That approach makes sense when finding a single piece of information is the goal. ⓑ However, understanding a difficult passage requires attention to the relationships between its ideas. ⓒ A familiar word can have a different meaning depending on the sentence around it. ⓓ A later paragraph may also limit a claim that seemed simple at first. ⓔ To understand a demanding text, readers should slow down enough to examine how its parts work together. Pausing to ask how an example supports a claim can reveal more than merely reaching the last line. Reading a sentence again may likewise help us see a connection that we missed. The point is to give the text the attention needed to construct its meaning.
solution: 글은 어려운 글을 이해하려면 문장과 문단 사이의 관계를 살피며 읽어야 한다고 주장한다. ⓑ는 이러한 읽기의 필요성을 설명하고, ⓔ는 그에 따른 핵심적인 읽기 태도까지 포괄하므로 주제문으로 가장 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 논의를 포괄하는 주제문을 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 고르시오.

Suppose a student wants to write a song unlike any song she has heard before. ⓐ She might initially believe that listening to other music would make her work less original. Yet avoiding every influence would also leave her with fewer musical possibilities to consider. ⓑ A rhythm from one piece could be joined to a pattern of sounds suggested by another. Neither source alone would determine the result; her choices would shape their relationship. ⓒ Creative originality often develops through the thoughtful rearrangement of familiar elements. ⓓ The same process can occur when a writer brings ideas from different readings into a new argument. ⓔ Encountering a wider variety of material therefore gives a creator more possibilities to explore. Such exposure does not produce an original work automatically. The creator must still select, alter, and connect what is available until it serves a new purpose.
solution: 노래와 글쓰기 사례는 익숙한 요소를 선택하고 새롭게 연결하는 과정에서 독창성이 생긴다는 설명을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 사례들을 포괄하는 일반적 진술인 ⓒ가 주제문이다. ⓔ는 이 원리에서 도출되는 실천적 시사점에 해당한다.

body:
다음 글에서 반론과 사례를 아우르며 글쓴이의 중심 주장을 제시하는 문장은?

A familiar ceremony can become difficult to perform when the lives of its participants change. ⓐ One response is to insist that every detail must be preserved, since any alteration might seem to weaken its connection with the past. Another is to remove whatever is inconvenient, even if little of the ceremony remains. Neither response asks which features make the practice meaningful to those who share it. ⓑ A tradition can retain its identity through change when adjustments preserve the relationships and meanings that make it worth continuing. ⓒ For instance, a shared meal might use different ingredients while continuing to bring generations together. ⓓ Conversely, keeping every dish exactly the same would accomplish little if the participants no longer understood why they gathered. ⓔ Attention to a custom's original form can still help people recognize what earlier generations valued. But that form provides guidance for judgment; it cannot replace judgment about how the practice can remain meaningful in present circumstances.
solution: 글은 전통의 모든 형식을 고수하는 태도와 편의에 따라 무조건 바꾸는 태도를 모두 검토한다. 중심 주장은 전통을 지속할 가치가 있게 만드는 관계와 의미를 보존하면서 변화해야 한다는 ⓑ이다. ⓔ는 과거의 형식에도 참고 가치가 있다는 보충 설명으로, 글 전체를 포괄하지는 않는다.

body:
다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 전체 논지를 가장 잘 집약한 주제문은?

Consider a diagram designed to explain how several ideas are related. ⓐ Adding every qualification might make the diagram more complete while making the main relationship harder to see. A simpler version could communicate that relationship clearly, yet fail to answer a different question requiring those qualifications. ⓑ It would therefore be misleading to rank the two versions solely by counting how many details each contains. ⓒ A simplified representation should be evaluated by whether its selections serve the question it is intended to answer. ⓓ This requires users to identify the task before deciding which omissions are acceptable. ⓔ It also requires them to notice when a new task calls for information that the representation excludes. A diagram useful for an introductory explanation need not be discarded because it cannot support a more detailed discussion. The mistake is to assume that success in the first task guarantees adequacy for the second.
solution: 글은 단순화한 표현의 가치를 포함된 정보의 양이 아니라 그것이 답하려는 질문과의 적합성으로 판단해야 한다고 설명한다. 이 평가 기준을 직접 제시하는 ⓒ가 주제문이다. ⓓ와 ⓔ는 그 기준에 따라 사용자가 수행해야 할 구체적인 판단을 각각 설명한다.

body:
다음 글에서 가상 사례를 설명하는 일반 원리를 제시하여 글 전체의 논지를 지탱하는 문장은?

Imagine that a school rewards teachers according to the number of written comments they leave on students' work. Initially, the count might offer a rough indication of how much individual attention students receive. ⓐ Once rewards depend on that count, however, a teacher could increase it by dividing one useful observation into several brief remarks without improving the guidance. ⓑ The resulting rise would show that the recording rule had been satisfied more fully, while leaving the educational value uncertain. A school might respond by requiring a minimum length for each comment, but that requirement would introduce another visible condition that could be met without addressing students' needs. ⓒ Such difficulties do not establish that written feedback is ineffective or that records should be abandoned. ⓓ When people are rewarded for a visible sign of quality, their efforts to produce the sign can weaken its reliability as evidence of the quality itself. ⓔ Reviewing whether comments actually help students revise their work would provide a way to check what the count alone cannot establish. The count may remain informative, provided its increase is treated as something to investigate rather than sufficient proof of improvement.
solution: 글은 피드백의 수를 보상 기준으로 삼으면 실제 교육적 가치와 무관하게 그 수만 늘어날 수 있다는 가상 사례를 제시한다. ⓓ는 이를 지표에 대한 보상이 그 지표의 증거 가치를 약화할 수 있다는 일반 원리로 설명한다. ⓑ는 사례에서 나타난 결과의 해석이고, ⓔ는 해당 문제를 점검하는 구체적인 방법이다.

body:
다음 글에서 도입의 통념, 이어지는 사례, 마지막의 조건을 모두 포괄하는 주제문은?

It is tempting to judge an explanation by how closely it resembles everything it explains. On that view, each omitted detail appears to be a defect waiting to be corrected. ⓐ The value of a simplified account lies in making a particular relationship understandable, provided that its omissions remain appropriate to the claims drawn from it. ⓑ A teacher introducing a complex idea may temporarily set aside exceptions so that students can follow its central structure. This need not imply that the exceptions are unimportant; their relevance depends on what the explanation is being used to establish. ⓒ If students later apply that account to a case in which an excluded condition matters, an earlier strength can become a source of error. ⓓ Making the limits explicit therefore helps users distinguish a legitimate extension of an explanation from an unsupported one. Yet attaching a warning to every omission would not by itself improve the account, since excessive qualification could conceal the relationship it was designed to reveal. ⓔ The appropriate level of detail must consequently be reconsidered whenever the scope of the intended conclusion changes. Neither completeness alone nor clarity alone settles the matter: the explanation must illuminate its subject without supporting conclusions that its chosen boundaries cannot justify.
solution: 글은 설명의 가치를 완전성만으로 판단하는 통념을 비판하면서, 단순화의 유용성과 그 적용 범위에 관한 조건을 함께 제시한다. ⓐ는 특정 관계를 이해시키는 기능과 생략이 도출되는 주장에 적절해야 한다는 조건을 모두 포함하므로 주제문이다. ⓓ와 ⓔ는 이 원리에서 파생되는 한계 명시와 세부 수준 재검토의 필요성을 각각 다룬다.

body:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

[주어진 문장]
These survivors reproduce, passing their resistance on to later generations.

Antibiotics can eliminate bacteria that cause many infections, but not every bacterium responds to a drug in the same way. (㉠) When an antibiotic is used, bacteria that are easily affected by it die. (㉡) A small number that can resist the drug, however, may remain alive. (㉢) As this process is repeated, resistant bacteria make up an increasingly large part of the population. (㉣) The medicine may then become much less effective than it once was. (㉤) Doctors therefore try to avoid prescribing antibiotics when they are not truly necessary.
solution: ‘These survivors’는 바로 앞 문장의 약물에 저항하여 살아남은 소수의 박테리아를 가리킨다. 이들이 번식한다는 내용 뒤에 내성 박테리아의 비율이 커진다는 결과가 이어지므로 ㉢이 정답이다.

body:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

[주어진 문장]
The label had altered the participants’ experience even though it had not altered the drink itself.

People often believe that enjoyment depends entirely on the actual quality of a product. (㉠) Their expectations, however, may become part of what they experience. (㉡) In a wine study, participants were shown price information while tasting several samples. (㉢) Some samples presented as differently priced products were, without the participants’ knowledge, the same wine. (㉣) Even so, the participants reported more pleasure when they thought that the wine cost more, and their brain activity showed a similar difference. (㉤) This influence of price helps explain why a luxury brand may hesitate to offer large discounts: a lower price could weaken the expectation that its product is special.
solution: 주어진 문장은 동일한 와인도 가격표에 따라 다르게 경험되었다는 실험 결과를 정리한다. 따라서 참가자의 반응이 제시된 뒤, 그 결과를 마케팅에 적용하는 내용이 나오기 전인 ㉤이 적절하다.

body:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

[주어진 문장]
What can be carried across languages, then, may be the purpose of the joke rather than the verbal device that originally achieved it.

A joke may appear to be a short and simple piece of language, yet it can present a translator with an unusually complex problem. (㉠) Its humor may depend on a word that has two meanings in the original language but only one in the target language. (㉡) It may also assume that listeners recognize a local custom or a familiar public figure. (㉢) A direct translation can therefore communicate the literal information while removing the very feature that made the line amusing. (㉣) For this reason, some translators invent a different joke that makes the new audience laugh at roughly the same point in the text. (㉤) Others preserve the original wording and explain it in a note, accepting that an explanation seldom produces the immediate response of humor.
solution: 주어진 문장은 말장치 자체는 옮기지 못하더라도 웃음을 유발하려는 목적은 옮길 수 있다는 결론이다. 앞에서는 직역으로 유머가 사라지는 문제가 제시되고, 뒤에서는 같은 효과를 내는 다른 농담을 만드는 해결책이 나오므로 ㉣이 적절하다.

body:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

[주어진 문장]
The inconvenience remained minor only while journeys were too slow for travelers to notice much conflict between one town’s clock and another’s.

Before standard time was introduced, communities commonly determined noon by observing when the sun reached its highest point. (㉠) Since that moment does not occur everywhere at once, neighboring towns could set their clocks several minutes apart. (㉡) Such local variation was manageable for much of human history. (㉢) Railways, however, allowed people and information to move rapidly across many towns. (㉣) A single train schedule now had to coordinate places whose clocks gave different times, creating both confusion and the risk of accidents. (㉤) Railway companies responded by using common times over large regions, and governments later adopted the system of time zones.
solution: 주어진 문장은 지역별 시각 차이가 이동 속도가 느릴 때에만 큰 문제가 아니었다고 설명한다. 이는 앞 문장의 ‘manageable’을 구체화하면서, 뒤의 철도 등장으로 상황이 달라지는 전환을 준비하므로 ㉢에 들어가야 한다.

body:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

[주어진 문장]
Where either regularity or reliable correction is missing, accumulated experience may strengthen confidence without improving judgment.

Experience is often treated as if its mere quantity guaranteed expertise, but the environment in which experience is acquired matters more than the number of years involved. (㉠) Accurate intuition can develop when events contain patterns that recur and when people quickly learn whether their predictions were correct. (㉡) Firefighters and chess players repeatedly encounter such conditions: meaningful signals appear again, and the consequences of earlier judgments can be examined. (㉢) A stock market does not provide the same learning structure. (㉣) Prices respond to numerous unpredictable influences, while the outcome of a decision may become clear only much later and may still reflect luck rather than insight. (㉤) Consequently, an investor’s strong feeling of certainty cannot by itself prove that genuine expertise has developed.
solution: 주어진 문장의 ‘regularity’와 ‘reliable correction’은 앞에서 제시한 반복되는 패턴과 신속한 피드백을 일반화한 표현이다. 이 문장은 그러한 조건이 없을 때의 결과를 제시하며, 바로 뒤의 주식시장이 그 조건을 충족하지 못하는 사례로 이어지므로 ㉢이 가장 적절하다.

body:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

[주어진 문장]
Paradoxically, therefore, an individual use that appears to end successfully can still contribute to the collective failure of the medicine.

The benefit of antibiotics is immediate and visible: a bacterial infection that once threatened a life may become treatable. (㉠) The cost of excessive use, by contrast, develops gradually across populations of bacteria and is therefore easier to overlook. (㉡) Each exposure removes susceptible bacteria while allowing resistant ones to survive and reproduce. (㉢) A patient may recover, so that particular treatment seems to have caused no broader harm. (㉣) Yet repeated use gives resistant bacteria more opportunities to spread, eventually making familiar drugs ineffective for other patients as well. (㉤) This gap between an apparent short-term benefit and a delayed shared cost is why antibiotics should be prescribed only when needed and taken exactly as directed.
solution: 주어진 문장은 한 환자의 성공적인 치료가 전체적으로는 약효 상실에 기여할 수 있다는 역설을 제시한다. 앞 문장의 개인적 회복과 뒤 문장의 내성 확산을 연결해야 하므로 ㉣이 적절하다. ‘individual use’와 ‘collective failure’의 대조도 전후 내용과 정확히 대응한다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Open offices are designed to make communication easier. Without walls between desks, employees are expected to exchange ideas naturally throughout the day. __________, some workers respond to the lack of privacy by wearing headphones and avoiding conversation. Simply placing people in the same room, therefore, does not necessarily make them cooperate more.
solution: 빈칸 앞에서는 개방형 사무실이 의사소통을 촉진할 것이라는 기대를 설명한다. 뒤에서는 오히려 직원들이 대화를 피하기도 한다는 상반된 결과가 나오므로 역접의 연결어 However가 적절하다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Navigation apps allow travelers to reach unfamiliar places with little effort. Yet users who merely obey every instruction may fail to notice street names or major buildings. __________, they arrive at the destination without developing a clear mental picture of the area. To improve their sense of direction, they should pay attention to the route instead of looking only at the screen.
solution: 주변의 거리와 건물을 살피지 않는 것이 원인이고, 지역에 대한 심적 지도를 형성하지 못하는 것이 그 결과이다. 따라서 결과를 나타내는 As a result가 알맞다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Researchers must be cautious when explaining animal behavior. An action that appears to express a human-like emotion may have a simpler cause. (A) __________, a dog may lower its body not because it understands that it has done something morally wrong, but because it recognizes an angry voice. Such caution helps prevent researchers from reading their own expectations into what they observe. (B) __________, caution should not become an automatic refusal to consider the possibility of animal emotions. Scientists need to examine that possibility while continuing to demand reliable evidence.
solution: (A) 뒤의 개 행동은 앞의 일반적인 주장을 구체화하는 사례이므로 For example이 적절하다. (B) 뒤에서는 신중함이 지나쳐서도 안 된다는 반대 측면을 제시하므로 Nevertheless가 알맞다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Planting a single high-yield crop variety can simplify farm work. All the plants mature at nearly the same time and can be handled in the same way. Uniformity in useful traits, however, usually means uniformity in weaknesses as well. (A) __________, if one plant is vulnerable to a particular disease, most of the field may be vulnerable to it too. A diverse field operates differently. Some varieties may be harmed, but others may possess traits that allow them to survive. (B) __________, diversity can prevent a single disease from destroying the entire harvest, even though it may make farming less convenient at first.
solution: (A) 뒤 문장은 유전적 약점까지 동일하다는 앞 내용을 구체적으로 다시 표현하므로 In other words가 적절하다. 여러 품종 중 일부가 살아남는 것은 전체 수확의 파괴를 막는 원인이 되므로 (B)에는 결과를 나타내는 Therefore가 들어가야 한다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

People sometimes pay for a long-term gym membership because they believe the expense will force them to exercise. (A) __________, the payment is made by the person they are today, while the effort must be supplied repeatedly by their future self. As daily demands accumulate, the memory of the payment may become less powerful than the attraction of resting at home. (B) __________, arranging to meet a friend at the gym can create a more immediate reason to show up: skipping the workout now means disappointing someone now. Effective plans often succeed by changing the situation surrounding a choice, not merely by increasing its financial cost.
solution: (A)에서는 선결제가 운동을 강제할 것이라는 믿음과 실제 행동 사이의 한계를 제시하므로 However가 적절하다. (B) 뒤의 친구와 약속하는 방법은 더 즉각적인 동기를 만드는 구체적인 사례이므로 For example이 알맞다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Punishing every workplace mistake may appear to strengthen responsibility. (A) __________, it can weaken the flow of information on which genuine safety depends. An employee who expects punishment has a reason to remain silent, so the organization loses the opportunity to discover a faulty procedure before it causes greater harm. A safer system therefore distinguishes carelessness from an honest error. (B) __________ treating the latter simply as an offense, the system encourages workers to report how it occurred. The report can then reveal problems in training, equipment, or routines that affect many other employees. (C) __________, reducing punishment in carefully defined cases may increase rather than decrease organizational responsibility.
choices: However …… Instead of …… In this sense
Likewise …… Instead of …… On the contrary
solution: (A)에는 처벌의 긍정적 외관과 정보 흐름을 약화시키는 실제 효과를 대조하는 However가 필요하다. (B)는 정직한 실수를 범죄처럼 처리하는 방식 대신 보고를 장려한다는 뜻이므로 Instead of가 적절하다. 마지막 문장은 앞의 논리를 요약하여 책임의 의미를 재해석하므로 In this sense가 가장 자연스럽다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Navigation technology can reduce the mental effort required to travel, but reduced effort is not identical to reduced ability. A person may use an app while still examining the route, identifying landmarks, and predicting the next turn. (A) __________, the important issue is not simply whether the technology is used, but how attention is distributed while it is being used. Step-by-step commands can discourage active observation when followed passively. (B) __________, the same commands can support learning when users compare them with what they see around them. (C) __________, abandoning navigation apps altogether is unnecessary; using them in a more attentive manner may preserve both convenience and spatial learning.
choices: In other words …… By contrast …… Therefore
As a result …… For instance …… Likewise
solution: (A)는 앞의 설명을 ‘사용 여부보다 사용 방식이 중요하다’는 핵심으로 바꾸어 말하므로 In other words가 적절하다. (B)에서는 수동적 사용의 부정적 효과와 능동적 사용의 학습 효과가 대조되므로 By contrast가 필요하다. 마지막은 이 대조에서 도출되는 결론이므로 Therefore가 알맞다.

body:
다음 안내문을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

Teen Reading Program

• Period: January 8–February 19
• Participants: Students aged 14–19 who have a library card
• Task: Finish four books and post a review of at least 120 words for each book on the library website.
• Printed books, e-books, and audiobooks are all accepted.
• Every student who completes the task receives a notebook.
• The closing event takes place on February 24. Its location will be announced later.
choices: What is the minimum age for participation?
How many books must participants finish?
Where will the closing event take place?

A written task list can free the mind from unnecessary work. If people try to remember every unfinished duty, those duties may repeatedly ⓐ**interrupt** their thoughts. It can also help them ⓒ**focus** on the activity in front of them. Of course, writing down a task does not ⓓ**complete** it, but it makes the task easier to manage. When a new technology makes an activity more convenient, people often begin to perform that activity more ⓐ**frequently**. In this way, the standard for what counts as a reasonable amount of work may ⓑ**change**. The minutes initially ⓒ**saved** by the technology are then occupied by additional duties. Learners sometimes judge a practice method by how smoothly the practice session proceeds. Repeating one type of problem can produce a quick sense of ⓐ**mastery**, since the same solution is used again and again. By contrast, alternating among several types forces learners to identify the nature of each problem before selecting a method. This repeated decision making may ⓑ**disrupt** the comfortable rhythm of practice and make immediate performance appear worse. Nevertheless, it can strengthen the learner's ability to ⓒ**distinguish** one problem type from another. The apparent difficulty of mixed practice therefore does not necessarily indicate a lack of learning. Indeed, the ease of repeated practice may ⓓ**conceal** weaknesses that become visible only when different problems are combined. Judging learning solely by short-term fluency is consequently a ⓔ**dependable** way to predict later performance.

A translation cannot avoid taking a position on the work it presents. Where the original permits several shades of meaning, the translator must often select an expression that gives some of them greater ⓐ**prominence** than others. The resulting version may be clear and convincing, but its clarity has been achieved partly by ⓑ**preserving** possibilities that the source text left open. This is why two careful translations can differ without either being careless. Their differences may reveal the distinct features of the original to which each translator was most ⓒ**sensitive**. Reading the versions together can therefore broaden rather than confuse our understanding, provided that we do not mistake any single version for an exhaustive account. The limitations of each translation are, in this sense, not merely ⓓ**defects**; they can help readers notice choices that would otherwise remain invisible. Variation among translations may thus become an interpretive ⓔ**resource**.

Such (D)(be) the confusion that several personal items were left behind. The fewer explanations the students received, the (E)(anxious) they became.
answer: (A) had  (B) Told  (C) to obey  (D) was  (E) more anxious
solution: Hardly가 문두에 오면 과거완료의 조동사가 도치되므로 (A)는 had이다. 학생들이 지시를 받은 것이므로 (B)는 수동의 과거분사 Told이고, ‘have no choice but to부정사’에 따라 (C)는 to obey이다. 단수 주어 the confusion에 맞춰 (D)는 was를 쓰며, 비교급 상관 구문이므로 (E)는 more anxious가 된다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Imagine finding a notebook you like in an online shop. At first, you decide to compare it with other notebooks before buying it. Then a message appears: this color will no longer be available after today. Suddenly, comparing prices seems less important than ordering immediately. Yet nothing about the notebook itself has changed. Its paper is no better, and its cover is no stronger. What has changed is your belief about whether you will have another chance to get it. Sellers can encourage this response by limiting the time during which an ordinary product is offered. The feeling of __________ can make the product seem more desirable, even when its practical value remains the same.
solution: 판매 종료 안내를 본 뒤 상품의 품질은 그대로인데도 구매 욕구가 커지는 상황이다. 구입 기회가 제한된다는 인식이 상품의 매력을 높이므로 빈칸에는 ‘희소성’을 뜻하는 scarcity가 적절하다.

body:
빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Suppose you send a friend a message asking, "Are you free?" If you have just discussed meeting after school, your friend will probably understand that you are asking about available time. If you have been discussing the cost of a service your friend provides, the same question may be understood as asking whether payment is required. The words alone do not settle the meaning. A reader needs to connect them with what came before and with the situation in which they appear. Therefore, when a short message seems strange or unclear, checking its __________ may be more useful than looking up each familiar word in a dictionary.
solution: 같은 질문도 앞서 나눈 대화와 사용된 상황에 따라 의미가 달라진다는 내용이다. 개별 단어의 뜻보다 주변 맥락을 확인해야 하므로 context가 적절하다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

Suppose a student wants to change the order of the subjects she studies each evening. She could spend several days trying to predict the perfect order, but a short trial would probably teach her more. If the new arrangement proves unhelpful, she can return to the old one the following week. Compare this with a choice that creates a long-lasting commitment and offers no simple way back. In that case, gathering information before acting deserves much greater attention. The important difference is not whether either choice might turn out badly; almost any choice can disappoint us. It is whether a disappointing result can be corrected at a reasonable cost. Before deciding how much thought a decision requires, we should therefore consider its __________.
solution: 글은 잘못될 가능성 자체보다 잘못된 선택을 합리적인 비용으로 되돌릴 수 있는지가 중요하다고 설명한다. 따라서 숙고의 정도를 정할 때 고려할 기준은 ‘되돌릴 수 있는 정도’를 뜻하는 reversibility이다.

body:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

A writing task that allows any subject, any length, and any form may look like an ideal invitation to be creative. Yet a student facing it may spend more time choosing among possibilities than developing one of them. Now imagine requiring the student to describe a familiar place without using any words that directly name colors. The task becomes narrower, but the student must discover other ways to make the scene vivid. This does not mean that every rule improves writing. A rule that leaves no meaningful choice can simply prevent expression. Useful __________ occupy the space between having no direction and having no room to move: they close some easy routes while leaving less obvious ones open. Their value lies in directing invention without determining its result.
solution: 빈칸 뒤에서는 쉬운 방법 일부를 막되 새로운 표현을 탐색할 여지는 남기는 조건을 설명한다. 모든 규칙이 도움이 된다는 뜻은 아니며, 창의성을 유도하는 적절한 ‘제약’이 핵심이므로 constraints가 정답이다.

body:
다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Consider two possible ways to design an online shopping basket. In one, removing an unwanted item requires several screens, while purchasing everything happens with a single touch. In the other, removing items is simple, but the final purchase requires the buyer to review the total and confirm it. Both designs contain an obstacle, so counting the number of steps tells us little about which design serves the buyer. We must ask what each obstacle interrupts. One delays the correction of an unwanted choice; the other interrupts a choice before it becomes a payment. Thus, __________ is not automatically a design failure. Placed at a moment when an impulse may conflict with a person's considered intention, it can help that person remain in control. Its usefulness depends on its location and purpose.
solution: 두 설계 모두 장애물을 포함하지만, 구매 취소를 방해하는지 충동적인 결제를 재고하게 하는지에 따라 가치가 달라진다. 따라서 무조건 설계의 실패로 볼 수 없는 것은 행동에 저항이나 번거로움을 더하는 friction이다.

body:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Imagine that a student states one conclusion after reading an initial set of observations and states the opposite after receiving additional observations. Someone comparing only the two statements might praise the student if they matched and criticize the student if they differed. But this judgment treats the conclusion as though it were independent of the grounds supporting it. If the grounds have changed substantially, repeating the earlier conclusion may require the student to abandon the very method that originally justified it. What appears to be loyalty to a belief can therefore conceal disloyalty to the process of judging evidence. Conversely, __________ at the level of stated conclusions may be necessary to preserve a stable commitment at the level of reasoning. This does not excuse changing an answer whenever it becomes inconvenient. The change is defensible only when the evidence, rather than the desire to escape criticism, explains it.
solution: 글은 진술한 결론의 일치와 증거를 판단하는 원칙의 일치를 구분한다. 증거가 바뀌면 추론 원칙을 유지하기 위해 오히려 결론에서는 ‘비일관성’이 나타날 수 있으므로 inconsistency가 적절하다. 마지막 두 문장은 이러한 변화가 편의가 아니라 증거에 근거해야 한다는 조건을 제시한다.

body:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Imagine a notice declaring that complaints about a service have doubled. The statement may be entirely accurate, yet it does not by itself establish that the service has become less reliable. The number of people using it might also have doubled, or the method of collecting complaints might have become more effective. These possibilities do not prove that reliability has remained unchanged. Rather, they show why the reported increase cannot settle the question on its own. A useful __________ supplies the conditions under which a fact can support one interpretation more strongly than another. It is therefore more than extra detail attached to a finished meaning. It helps determine what the fact is evidence of in the first place. Removing it can leave every reported number correct while allowing a conclusion that the complete information would not justify.
solution: 민원 수의 증가만으로 서비스 신뢰도 하락을 단정할 수 없으며, 이용자 수나 수집 방식 등의 조건을 함께 알아야 한다. 빈칸에는 사실이 어떤 해석의 근거가 되는지 판단하게 해 주는 ‘맥락’을 뜻하는 context가 적절하다. 글은 숫자의 정확성과 그 숫자에서 도출한 결론의 타당성이 별개임을 강조한다.

body:
다음 글의 흐름에서 벗어나는 문장을 고르시오.

An empty moment does not always need to be filled. When nothing immediately demands our attention, we may begin thinking about things beyond our present surroundings. ⓐ An unfinished plan or an old memory can enter our thoughts during such a pause. ⓑ Ideas that seemed separate may then meet in an unexpected way. ⓒ This is why a short period of boredom can sometimes make room for a creative thought. ⓓ People are often advised to exercise regularly to maintain their physical health. ⓔ Reaching for a phone at every quiet moment, however, may interrupt this useful movement of the mind. If we always give our attention to another message or video, we leave fewer opportunities for ideas to develop on their own. Allowing an occasional empty moment may therefore be more valuable than immediately escaping it.
solution: 이 글은 지루하고 조용한 시간이 생각의 연결과 창의적 사고에 도움이 될 수 있다는 내용이다. ⓓ는 신체 건강을 위한 규칙적인 운동을 권하는 문장으로, 이러한 흐름에서 벗어난다.

body:
다음 글에서 문맥상 어울리지 않는 문장은?

A language can grow through contact with people who speak other languages. Speakers sometimes meet an unfamiliar idea and adopt the word that others already use for it. ⓐ In this way, a word can cross a language boundary along with the idea it names. ⓑ Many people think that children find it easier than adults to learn a foreign language. ⓒ After the word enters its new language, its pronunciation or grammatical form may change. ⓓ Eventually, people may use it comfortably without knowing where it first came from. ⓔ Tracing such words backward can therefore reveal earlier connections between different communities. The words people use every day may carry signs of cultural contact that their speakers no longer recognize.
solution: 글은 다른 언어의 단어가 유입되고 정착하는 과정과 그 단어가 보여 주는 문화적 접촉을 설명한다. ⓑ는 외국어 학습의 용이성을 나이에 따라 비교하므로 단어 차용이라는 중심 내용과 관계가 없다.

body:
다음 글에서 전체적인 논리 전개와 관계없는 문장을 고르시오.

A surprising research headline should begin a reader's inquiry rather than end it. What matters is how the reported finding fits with the evidence already available. ⓐ Coffee shops provide spaces where people can read, work, or talk about subjects that interest them. ⓑ Even a carefully conducted investigation may produce a result that partly reflects chance or the particular participants involved. ⓒ A finding becomes more convincing when other researchers obtain similar results under different conditions. ⓓ Agreement across several investigations gives readers a stronger reason for confidence than one striking announcement does. ⓔ When reports appear to conflict, readers should therefore consider the wider pattern before revising their beliefs. This approach allows them to remain open to new information while avoiding an immediate change of habit every time a dramatic headline appears.
solution: 글의 중심은 개별 연구를 보도한 제목만으로 판단하지 말고 여러 연구의 증거를 종합해야 한다는 것이다. ⓐ는 사람들이 읽거나 대화하는 장소로서 커피숍을 소개하므로 연구 결과의 신뢰성을 판단하는 논의와 연결되지 않는다.

body:
다음 글의 주제 전개에서 벗어나는 문장은?

A performer's repeated preparation can be useful even when it cannot determine the result. Consider a student who arranges a pencil and an eraser in a particular order before an examination. ⓐ The arrangement does not supply any answers, but completing it may make the situation feel less uncertain. ⓑ Whereas the questions remain unknown, the familiar sequence offers a small action whose beginning and end the student can manage. ⓒ This contrast can help explain why a simple routine brings a sense of control under pressure. ⓓ That feeling may help the student settle down and direct attention toward the work ahead. ⓔ In televised tennis, the visibility of the ball is also an important consideration, which partly explains the adoption of yellow balls. The value of preparation of this kind thus lies in how it steadies the performer before an uncertain outcome.
solution: 글은 일정한 준비 행동이 통제감을 제공하여 수행 전 긴장을 가라앉히는 원리를 설명한다. ⓔ는 수행 상황과 관련된 표현을 사용하지만, 내용은 방송에서 공이 잘 보이도록 하는 색상 선택에 관한 것이므로 준비 의식의 심리적 기능과 관계없다.

body:
다음 글에서 전체 흐름상 제외하는 것이 가장 적절한 문장은?

The apparent familiarity of a word can hide evidence of a language's past. A borrowed expression may become so ordinary that speakers no longer recognize it as an arrival from elsewhere. ⓐ Changes in its sound and grammatical behavior can help it blend into its new surroundings. ⓑ Its present form may consequently seem to belong entirely to the language in which it is now used. ⓒ For a learner, however, beginning a second language in childhood is often believed to be easier than beginning it later in life. ⓓ Investigating the expression's origin can nevertheless reveal an earlier encounter between communities. ⓔ Across many such expressions, these encounters form a record of contact through trade, migration, or cultural exchange. Everyday vocabulary can therefore preserve a history that is not immediately visible to the people using it.
solution: 글은 차용어가 새 언어에 동화되어 기원이 드러나지 않더라도 과거의 문화적 접촉을 간직한다는 내용이다. ⓒ의 however는 대조 관계를 만드는 듯하지만 실제로는 논의 대상을 단어의 역사에서 개인의 외국어 학습 시기로 바꾼다. ⓒ를 제외하면 차용어의 현재 모습과 그 기원을 조사했을 때 드러나는 역사적 의미가 자연스럽게 연결된다.

body:
다음 글에서 논지의 일관성을 해치는 문장을 고르시오.

When people judge a danger, the ease of recalling an example may quietly take the place of evidence about its frequency. The resulting judgment can feel reasonable because a clear image seems to offer something concrete to rely on. ⓐ Yet the clarity of that image may reflect the attention an incident received rather than how often such incidents occur. ⓑ To evaluate an aircraft's protection against failure, however, one relevant consideration is whether backup equipment can take over when a component stops working. ⓒ An unusual accident repeatedly shown in reports may consequently remain easier to imagine than a familiar kind of accident that attracts little notice. ⓓ If this difference in mental accessibility guides the comparison, the less frequent danger may appear more likely. ⓔ The confidence of the judgment then comes partly from the availability of a remembered example, without a corresponding basis in the underlying frequencies. Correcting the judgment requires asking whether the example is easy to retrieve because it is typical or because it has been made especially memorable.
solution: 글은 사고 사례를 쉽게 떠올리는 정도가 실제 발생 빈도의 판단을 대신하는 인지적 편향을 설명한다. ⓑ는 항공기 위험이라는 관련 소재를 다루지만, 기억과 판단의 관계가 아니라 장비 고장에 대비한 항공기의 실제 보호 기능을 평가하는 기준을 제시한다. ⓑ를 삭제하면 사고가 받은 관심이 기억의 접근성을 높이고, 이것이 빈도 판단을 왜곡한다는 인과관계가 이어진다.

body:
다음 글을 쓴 필자의 제안으로 가장 적절한 것은?

Imagine a neighborhood where the library is just across the road, but reaching it on foot requires a long walk to the nearest crossing. A driver may barely notice this arrangement, while a child or an older resident faces a real difficulty. A street plan should not be called successful simply because vehicles move smoothly through it. Before approving changes to a neighborhood road, city planners should check whether residents can comfortably reach the places they use every day. Safe crossings near these destinations and enough space to walk and rest deserve priority. A few minutes saved by drivers should not outweigh the everyday needs of people on foot. Planning should begin with the experience of walking through the neighborhood.
choices: 도서관 등 공공시설을 차량 통행이 적은 지역으로 이전해야 한다.
도로를 계획할 때 주민의 안전하고 편리한 보행을 우선 고려해야 한다.
차량의 이동 시간을 줄이기 위해 횡단보도 사이의 간격을 넓혀야 한다.
보행자의 편의를 위해 주거 지역의 모든 차량 진입을 금지해야 한다.
도로 이용의 불편을 줄이기 위해 주민에게 운전을 권장해야 한다.
solution: 필자는 차량이 원활히 이동한다는 이유만으로 도로 계획이 성공적이라고 볼 수 없다고 말한다. 주민이 일상적으로 이용하는 장소까지 안전하고 편리하게 걸어갈 수 있는지를 먼저 고려해야 한다는 주장이므로 ②가 정답이다.

body:
다음 글의 필자가 권하는 칭찬 방식으로 가장 적절한 것은?

After a student finishes a presentation, a teacher may say that it was wonderful. The student is pleased, but may still have no idea which part deserves to be used again. A more helpful response would identify a particular choice: the student explained an unfamiliar term before using it, so the audience could follow the discussion. This kind of praise does more than express approval. It connects an action with its value and gives the learner a clear direction for future work. Teachers do not need to make their praise longer or more frequent. They need to make it informative. When praising students, name the successful choice and explain how it helped.
choices: 학생의 자신감을 높이도록 가능한 한 자주 칭찬해야 한다.
발표 내용의 장점보다 학생의 타고난 능력을 칭찬해야 한다.
학생들이 경쟁하도록 다른 학생보다 우수한 점을 칭찬해야 한다.
칭찬의 효과를 높이도록 잘한 점과 부족한 점을 같은 비중으로 말해야 한다.
학생이 잘한 행동과 그 행동이 도움이 된 이유를 구체적으로 말해야 한다.
solution: 필자는 막연한 칭찬만으로는 학생이 어떤 부분을 다음에도 활용해야 할지 알기 어렵다고 설명한다. 성공적인 행동을 짚고 그것이 어떤 도움을 주었는지 알려 주라는 마지막 문장이 핵심이므로 ⑤가 정답이다.

body:
다음 글의 논지를 바탕으로 할 때, 필자가 지지할 교육 방침으로 가장 적절한 것은?

Written comments on an assignment are useful only if students do something with them. Yet classroom routines often separate receiving advice from having a chance to use it: one task is returned just as another begins. It is tempting to respond by writing even more detailed comments, but additional advice cannot solve the problem of having no opportunity to act. Teachers should build a revision stage into the assignment itself. Students might submit an improved version together with a short explanation of how they used the feedback. The original submission would still require serious effort, since meaningful revision depends on having something substantial to reconsider. What changes is the role of assessment. Instead of marking the point at which work must stop, it becomes a step that helps students continue learning.
choices: 학생이 피드백을 적용해 과제를 수정하고 그 내용을 설명하는 단계를 마련한다.
과제의 수정 기회를 제공하는 대신 첫 제출물에 대한 논평의 양을 늘린다.
첫 제출의 부담을 줄이기 위해 미완성 과제에도 완성된 과제와 같은 점수를 준다.
피드백을 스스로 해석하도록 교사의 설명 없이 새 과제를 반복해서 부여한다.
평가가 학습을 방해하지 않도록 모든 과제에 대한 점수와 논평을 없앤다.
solution: 필자는 논평의 양보다 학생이 그 논평을 실제로 활용할 기회가 있는지가 중요하다고 본다. 따라서 과제 수행 과정에 수정 단계와 피드백 활용에 대한 설명을 포함하는 ①을 지지할 것이다. 첫 제출에도 충실한 노력이 필요하다고 했으므로 수정 기회를 초기 과제의 부실함을 허용하는 것으로 이해해서는 안 된다.

body:
다음 글의 관점에서 의사결정을 평가하는 원칙으로 가장 적절한 것은?

Consider two managers choosing how to introduce a product. One compares the available options and considers possible problems; the other selects an option without examining them. If the second manager happens to achieve higher sales, it is easy to assume that the second decision was better. But this comparison mixes up what a person controlled with what became clear only afterward. Results matter: they can reveal weaknesses in our assumptions and help improve later choices. They cannot, however, establish by themselves whether an earlier choice was reasonable. That requires reconstructing the information and alternatives available when the choice was made. We should use outcomes to learn, while judging the original decision by the quality of the reasoning that could reasonably have supported it then. Otherwise, we may teach people to repeat an unjustified choice merely because it once worked.
choices: 판단 과정이 충분히 신중했다면 실패한 결과에서 얻을 교훈을 찾지 않아야 한다.
결정 당시의 정보가 부족했다면 실제 성과만으로 결정의 합리성을 판단해야 한다.
결과는 향후 학습에 활용하되, 결정의 타당성은 당시 정보와 추론을 중심으로 평가해야 한다.
좋은 성과를 낸 선택은 사전에 검토가 부족했더라도 같은 상황에서 반복하도록 권장해야 한다.

A researcher explaining a finding can mislead an audience without saying anything false. Presenting a conclusion in a confident voice while leaving its limitations unmentioned may encourage listeners to treat a provisional answer as a permanent one. Yet the opposite response—listing every unanswered question without explaining what the evidence does support—can be equally unhelpful. It leaves the audience unable to distinguish a well-supported conclusion from a guess. Responsible communication therefore requires more than admitting that mistakes are possible. Researchers should explain the strength of the current evidence, identify the uncertainties that matter to interpreting it, and indicate why later evidence might change the conclusion. This does not require delaying every announcement until doubt disappears. It requires giving people enough context to understand both why a claim deserves attention now and why revising it later need not mean that the earlier explanation was dishonest.
choices: 대중의 혼란을 줄이기 위해 결론을 바꿀 가능성이 있는 연구는 발표하지 않아야 한다.
과학의 잠정적 성격을 강조하기 위해 모든 연구 결론을 추측과 같은 수준으로 소개해야 한다.
연구의 신뢰성을 유지하기 위해 결론을 먼저 확정적으로 제시하고 한계는 수정 시점에 밝혀야 한다.
현재 근거의 강도와 해석에 중요한 불확실성을 함께 설명하여 결론의 수정 가능성을 이해시켜야 한다.
연구의 투명성을 확보하기 위해 결론의 근거보다 해결되지 않은 질문을 빠짐없이 나열하는 데 집중해야 한다.
solution: 필자는 한계를 숨겨 확정적인 인상을 주는 방식과, 근거가 뒷받침하는 내용은 설명하지 않은 채 미해결 문제만 나열하는 방식을 모두 비판한다. 현재 근거가 얼마나 강한지와 어떤 불확실성이 중요한지를 함께 전달해야 한다는 것이 핵심이므로 ④가 정답이다. 이는 발표를 무기한 미루거나 모든 결론을 단순한 추측으로 취급하라는 뜻이 아니다.
